attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Faithful: two present-tense observations, that it is not reliable enough and has no clear business model yet. Unhedged, so it can be scored.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary. Requiring credible viability for 'clear business model' fits his costs-and-revenue context. Q1 2024 is the evaluator's window. Assessing the two parts separately is reasonable.

evidence.note: March 2024 investigation found SGE recommending scam sites. This supports a reliability concern but gives no error rate. Google said these were uncommon queries. Says nothing on the business model.
Alphabet's January 2024 disclosure on SGE ad experiments. Company statement that does not tie returns to costs, so it neither shows nor rules out viability.

reviews.rationale: The reliability part has one documented set of serious failures but no evidence of how widespread they were. On commercial viability, the packet has only a company ad disclosure and nothing connecting monetisation to costs. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met for either part.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Verbatim, unhedged observation about how customers received Copilot.

contract.note: Reading 'not thrilled' as broadly lukewarm reception of Microsoft 365 Copilot is fair given the context. Q1 2024 window and the product choice are the evaluator's interpretation.

evidence.note: February 2024 summary of WSJ reporting: mixed reviews, with doubts about cost and errors among some testers, alongside reported efficiency gains. Shows nothing about how common these views were.
March 2024 report of customers complaining that Copilot falls short of ChatGPT. Very short text with no sample or product detail.
Microsoft-run survey of 1,300 users reporting productivity benefits. Includes employees, has no fieldwork cutoff and measures benefit rather than enthusiasm. Company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: Reports show mixed reviews and some complaints in Q1 2024 but have no customer count or sampling method. Microsoft's survey points the other way but is company-sponsored and indirect. No representative evidence settles whether reception was broadly lukewarm, so the contract's conditions are not met.
